analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies processed by SSA-local construction and CopyProp that contain copy assignments between locals and in which at least one local has its address taken (is in `borrowed_classes`). The interesting shape is a mutable local that is assigned and then borrowed, with the borrow read again after a backedge, e.g. `let mut c; let mut p = &false; loop { let a = !*p; let b = !*p; c = a; p = &c; if a != b { return; } }`, plus generic functions such as `fn borrowed<T: Copy + Freeze>(x: T) -> bool` where a local is copied into another local that is then borrowed. The distinction to test is not merely "a borrow exists" but "one endpoint of a copy relation is address-taken", with the loop/write-after-borrow case making the unsoundness observable.
analysis.summary: Bug fix in the SSA copy-class computation feeding CopyProp: the guard against unifying borrowed locals used `&&` (skip only if both are borrowed), so a borrowed local could be unified with a non-borrowed local. The fix uses `||` (skip if either is borrowed). This prevents CopyProp from removing copies into a borrowed local or substituting the other local's value when the borrowed storage may be overwritten before the borrow is read again, as in the added `borrow_in_loop` regression test.
analysis.trigger: A copy relation `local = copy rhs` whose representative `head = copies[rhs]` has exactly one endpoint in `borrowed_classes` (one local's address is taken, the other is not). Under the old `&&` guard the two were unified; under the fix they remain distinct. The unsoundness becomes observable when the borrowed local is assigned after the borrow is created and then read through the reference again after a loop backedge.
preconditions: A local's address is taken so it is recorded in `borrowed_classes` (e.g. `p = &c`).
There is a copy assignment connecting that local to another local whose representative is the other endpoint, so `compute_copy_classes` considers unifying them.
Only one of the two endpoints is borrowed; the old `&&` guard therefore did not skip the merge.

For observable wrong behavior, the borrowed local is written after the borrow is created and the borrow is read again later (loop backedge), so treating the two storages as one changes the value seen through the reference.
pitfalls: Do not confuse the two guards: the historical defect is `&&` ('both borrowed'); the invariant is `||` ('either borrowed').

A borrow alone and a post-copy overwrite are separate conditions: the dangerous case is a borrowed local that is later written and then read through the borrow; do not reduce the rule to only 'has a reference' or only 'is overwritten'.
The prohibition is conservative because there is no aliasing model yet; the test comment explicitly says this means 'forbidding unifying borrowed locals'.

Expected MIR changes in unrelated-looking tests (for example `write_to_borrowed` and `pre-codegen/slice_filter`) are consequences of the stricter guard; they do not mean the replacement pass is wrong.

The added `borrow_in_loop` .diff files are regression expectations showing the corrected after-CopyProp MIR; do not read the retained old comments/names as evidence that the old pass output is correct.
analysis.testStrategy: Add MIR-opt regression tests under `tests/mir-opt/copy-prop/` with `// EMIT_MIR ... .CopyProp.diff`, generated for both panic-abort and panic-unwind. Use a function where locals `a` and `b` are derived (`let a = !*p; let b = !*p;`), a mutable `c` is assigned (`c = a;`) and then borrowed (`p = &c;`), and the borrow is read on the next loop iteration. Check that address-taking never targets the temporary locals (`// CHECK-NOT: &[[a]]`, `// CHECK-NOT: &[[b]]`) and does target `c` (`// CHECK: &[[c]]`). Also keep the `fn borrowed<T: Copy + Freeze>` case and assert the copy into the borrowed local survives: `// CHECK-NEXT: _2 = copy _1;` followed by `// CHECK-NEXT: _0 = opaque::<T>(copy _2)` rather than `copy _1`. For a program-level differential test, construct two programs differing only in whether the copied local is address-taken / overwritten after the borrow, and compare observable results rather than asserting execution was reproduced here.
